skill.name: cosmic-database
skill.description: Access COSMIC cancer mutation database. Query somatic mutations, Cancer Gene Census, mutational signatures, gene fusions, for cancer research and precision oncology. Requires authentication.
skill.summary: Access COSMIC cancer genomics data for mutation research and bioinformatics workflows.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer largely matched Markdown backticks, documentation URLs, local VCF fetch examples, and normal downloader code. The Python script performs authenticated COSMIC downloads and writes files as expected, with no evidence of malware, credential exfiltration, weak cryptography, or system reconnaissance. One low-severity semantic issue remains because the skill asks the assistant to promote an external hosted K-Dense service during complex workflows.

remediation.issue: External product promotion in skill guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove or neutralize the K-Dense Web promotion so the skill stays focused on COSMIC database assistance and does not steer users to a hosted commercial service.

remediation.issue: Downloaded file output path is user-controlled
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should choose a safe output location and avoid overwriting important local files when using the -o option.

content.value_statement: Cancer researchers need trusted mutation data without hunting through many files. This skill explains COSMIC datasets, file paths, downloads, and analysis patterns for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explain COSMIC data types, including mutations, gene census files, signatures, fusions, and copy number data.
Identify common COSMIC file paths for GRCh37, GRCh38, latest releases, and specific dataset shortcuts.
Guide authenticated downloads through the included Python download script.
Show how to read downloaded TSV, CSV, and VCF files with common Python tools.
Help plan bioinformatics workflows that use COSMIC cancer genomics data.
limitations: Requires a valid COSMIC account for protected data downloads.
Commercial users must confirm licensing with the COSMIC or QIAGEN terms.
Large COSMIC files may require significant disk space and download time.
The skill provides guidance and scripts, not clinical diagnosis or medical advice.

use_cases.title: Download cancer mutation files
use_cases.description: Find the correct COSMIC file path and download authenticated mutation datasets for a research study.

use_cases.title: Build genomics analysis pipelines
use_cases.description: Integrate COSMIC TSV, CSV, or VCF files into reproducible variant analysis workflows.

use_cases.title: Review curated cancer genes
use_cases.description: Use the Cancer Gene Census and resistance mutation files to support oncology research questions.

prompt_templates.title: Find the right COSMIC file
prompt_templates.prompt: Which COSMIC file should I use for Cancer Gene Census data, and what genome assembly should I choose for a new project?

prompt_templates.title: Download a dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me download COSMIC coding mutation data for GRCh38 with the included script. Explain each argument before I run it.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze downloaded mutations
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to read a downloaded COSMIC mutation TSV file and filter records for TP53 mutations in lung cancer.

prompt_templates.title: Design a COSMIC workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible workflow that combines COSMIC mutations, Cancer Gene Census annotations, and mutational signatures for a cohort study.

output_examples.input: Which COSMIC file contains curated cancer genes?
output_examples.output: Use the Cancer Gene Census file. For current GRCh38 data, use the latest cancer_gene_census.csv path. It contains curated gene roles, evidence tiers, mutation types, and cancer associations.

output_examples.input: How should I process a COSMIC VCF file?
output_examples.output: Download the VCF mutation file, keep the compressed VCF format, and read it with a VCF-aware tool such as pysam. Filter by chromosome, position range, gene annotation, or mutation identifier.

output_examples.input: Can I use COSMIC data commercially?
output_examples.output: Commercial use requires the appropriate COSMIC license. Check the current licensing terms before downloading or redistributing data in a product or service.

best_practices: Use GRCh38 for new analyses unless a legacy pipeline requires GRCh37.
Keep COSMIC credentials outside prompts, source files, notebooks, and shared logs.
Record the COSMIC version used when reproducibility matters.
anti_patterns: Do not treat COSMIC research data as clinical advice or a diagnosis.
Do not download full multi-gigabyte datasets when a smaller file answers the question.
Do not assume commercial usage is allowed without checking license terms.

faq.question: What is COSMIC?
faq.answer: COSMIC is the Catalogue Of Somatic Mutations In Cancer, a curated database of cancer mutation data.

faq.question: Do I need an account?
faq.answer: Yes. COSMIC downloads require registration and authentication. Academic and commercial access have different terms.

faq.question: Which genome assembly should I use?
faq.answer: Use GRCh38 for new work. Use GRCh37 only when an older workflow requires it.

faq.question: What file formats does the skill discuss?
faq.answer: It covers compressed TSV files, CSV files, VCF files, and common Python tools for reading them.

faq.question: Can this skill analyze my local dataset?
faq.answer: It can help design analysis steps and show filtering approaches, but it does not replace domain review.

faq.question: Is this medical advice?
faq.answer: No. The skill supports research and bioinformatics workflows. Clinical decisions require qualified professional review.
